label: rem:weight-space-decomposition
title: Weight-space decomposition of the harmonic basis
html:
The adjoint bundle \mathrm{ad} \mathcal{S}_n has fibre \mathfrak{su}(2). Via the weight-space decomposition of \mathrm{SU}(2), the harmonic basis of \mathcal{H}^1(\mathcal{S}_n, \mathrm{ad} \mathcal{S}_n) splits into two families.

Longitudinal modes. These forms constitute the \mathrm{U}(1) backbone. They take values in the Cartan subalgebra of \mathfrak{su}(2) and have the geometric form \vartheta^0 \otimes H, where H is the diagonal generator. They represent steady-state laminar flows aligned with the \mathrm{U}(1) subgroup. If the bundle splits at a monodromy fixed point, these are the only modes that survive; they correspond to the magnetic flux of the stable vortices.

Ladder modes. These are the raising and lowering vortices. They take values in the off-diagonal generators E_\pm of \mathfrak{su}(2) and have the geometric form \vartheta^\pm \otimes E_\pm. They describe entangling flows that twist the \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) fibre along the brane. These modes generate the non-commutativity in the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) algebra (direct limit algebra).

In the 1-jet bundle J^1 \mathcal{S}_n (J^1\mathcal{S} local states), each basis element \alpha is a pair consisting of a value (the direction of the \mathrm{SU}(2) flow in the fibre) and a momentum (the gradient of that flow relative to the complex structure of the brane).
